I read that in other reviews but thought it was referring to size - no its quite large just really dingy and grimey looking. Maybe that's supposed to be cool? Honestly I wouldn't even mind if the food blew my socks off which it didn't. However there's a new donut place next door with the best donuts in the world.

Although they do provide $10 in drinks @ Cin Cin or 2-1 chip money. Wireless internet in the hotel is acceptable. It's just not free. But who goes to a casino to browse the Internet, right?The staff is extremely friendly. We were greeted daily by the security personnel who guards the elevators to the towers. To celebrate the Chinese New Year, the buffet theme was Chinese food. If you're going just for the Chinese food, don't bother. Go for what they they are known for -- steak, pot roast, fried chicken, shrimp, salad, especially dessert!

text_raw: We were walking through Nashville for a nice breakfast place, when we came upon D'Andrews. Very different from other cafes we had come across, D'Andrews had a open, light vibe, contrary to the heavy, dark atmosphere of a lot of restaurants around. The most windows I had seen in the area for one place. The food was just as good. It was a bakery and there was croissants and pastries, that looked(and tasted) delicious. On top of that, they had sandwiches of equal stature. The bread was soft and the falafel of my sandwich was crispy, and it all went so well together. We were tempted to ask if they were selling their bread. I looked over and saw my parents veggie sandwich. The egg literally oozed out the back, in a way that my dad had been trying to perfect, which says it all. Whenever I am in Nashville again, I will be sure to check this place out for a sweet or savory treat at brunch.

text_raw: Experiences like the one we had last night just remind me that we should stick to Nashville's long standing best restaurants and not try the newbies when celebrating an important occasion. Went in for my daughters' 16th birthday. My husband picked this place because he saw that there were other locations in the NYC area and figured the food would have to be good. He was also thinking our girls would like the gorgeous and Instagram-friendly decor. I went in expecting a higher-end experience (given the pricy menu), but what we got was a glammed up sports bar for "girls," as my daughters said. Had reservations and was surprised to find the restaurant dead, as this is usually not the case with Nashville's better restaurants. The hostess had her back to us when we entered and in spite of me yelling "excuse me" multiple times, the music was SO loud that she couldn't hear me and was startled to see us when she turned around. These two things, as well as the fact that most staff were unmasked and there are TVs on every surface should have been out clue to exit. But we had to put a deposit down on our reservation, so we stayed. Anyway, on to service. Our waitress left us sitting unattended for 15 minutes. I actually got out of the booth and asked the bartender to put in an appetizer order for us because she was not busy (only 3 people at the huge bar) and we were ravenous. She was super-nice and did this, no problem. Waitress finally came over and was clearly harried and pushy about getting our drink order (Including leaning over me and touching my phone without asking me to pull up the drink list). Later she did apologize about the wait and said that she had tables leaving "all at once". Being that the place was not busy, I'm not sure why another employee didn't help her out. Poor training and management?Ok- now food. It was mediocre at best. The highly recommended steak grilled cheese was so heavy and buttery that my daughter took 3 bites and felt sick. Cajun pasta had an unexpected cheesy base - like a mac and cheese vibe (dish was described as "creamy" and not "cheesy"). Neither ate their food. My husband got short rib pasta, which was unimpressive and tasted like it was made with jar sauce. My risotto was a cold gelatinous blob with overcooked chicken on top (ironically called airline chicken and it tasted like it too!). I did have some reservations about ordering risotto in a glorified sports bar, but at $38 and a guarantee from the waitress that it would be "delicious," I took a chance. I should have followed my gut and got a burger. The only standout thing about the meal were the absolutely delicious tomatoes in my risotto. With all the amazing restaurants in Nashville, we will definitely not be returning here. This is more of a place for drunken bachelorettes who care more about drinks and selfies than decent food. It's the kind of place I'd expect to find on lower Broadway, not out in Nashville proper and I will be very surprised if this place is still in business in three years. Maybe bachelorettes and tourists will keep them afloat, but I don't think they will be able to build a loyal local clientele. We expect better and know that Nashville has some truly amazing restaurants. Unfortunately, this is not one of them. Between ignoring the fact that we were celebrating a milestone birthday, music so loud that conversation was difficult, the mediocre food / service, the pricy menu and the lack of COVID-safe protocols, this will not be on our rotation list.

text_raw: They have two sections: one for boiled seafood and another for hot/fried food items. And they also sell Chinese food! This is the true hustle, and I totally respect that.I purchased 3 pounds of crawfish and some corn for $17. I was blown away because back home, crawfish is like $9.99/lb. The crawfish were big, some even huge, and so sweet! They were perfectly spicy from the sauce they were boiled in. Sooo good. We also got some boudin and gumbo! I liked their gumbo a lot. It was packed with seafood and seasoned pretty aggressively, which I loved. The boudin was ok, I like mine crisped up on the outside and they just give it to you boiled which isn't my favorite texture. If I'm in NOLA again, I will definitely come back for the seafood! This seems to be a favorite spot of the locals too, we came on a Friday evening and it was packed!

I was literally licking my fingers.I will be back I called Nicodimus and thanked him for giving me life this Sunday afternoon.

When you first walk in, of course the first thing you notice is the daily selection of cupcakes. I was excited to see they had an Egg Nog Cupcake. I love Egg Nog, so I knew that was the one I wanted. However, we had to have lunch first.Our lunches get two thumbs up, I was amazed at the quality and quantity we received. We started out with the Famous Barr's French Onion Soup, a great start to any lunch. As our sandwiches we selected the Monte Cristo and The Cubano. They were plentiful, and better then some that I have seen at popular Tea Rooms. As we feasted on our fabulous lunch, there was a steady stream of patrons coming in and getting cupcakes. text_raw: The hubs and I visited Miguel's yesterday after a surprisingly brief visit to the Apple Store. I was really excited to see how busy it was, as I remember that Johnny Carino's was typically a ghost town. As per usual, we found a seat at the bar.We started off with a margarita (strawberry blended) and an order of guacamole. The guacamole had a great texture and flavor, but it was WAY under-salted. As in, I salted every bite before I put it in my mouth-hole. Same thing goes for the chips. The salsa was pretty good, a little less hot than I might like it but I understand that it has to be made for the masses of tender-tongued Reno folk.The margarita tasted great and had a decent tequila flavor, and I appreciate that they take the time to make each margarita individually, rather than having a big machine that does it. There was a mix-up with the drinks but the bartenders fixed it quickly and with a smile. We ordered our food and waited. It seemed like it took a LONG time for the food to come. I didn't clock it, but I would estimate it took about 30 minutes or so. Which, if I'm ordering something that has to be baked to order I can somewhat understand, but Mexican food always seems to come out very quickly. Not sure what the problem was. I ordered a ground beef taco and a pork tamale combo; the hubs got a ground beef chimichanga. Talking about it on our way home, we decided that it wasn't that the food was *bad.* It just didn't taste like anything. I might as well have been eating cardboard. I couldn't pinpoint where the lack of flavor was (I continued to salt), but it's one of the meals that I think wasn't worth the calories. I hope this is just some growing pains, I know they're new, so I might give it a shot after awhile one night when I'm down there for a movie.

text_raw: I can't say enough good things about Amato Bros. The atmosphere is welcoming, like you're hanging out in a friend's basement bar, but with better food & good drinks. The staff, especially Chris, the bartender/manager, is super colloquial & I find myself excited to see him behind the bar because he's just a cool dude to chat with while we're dining/drinking. There's always a good beer selection, but even the seasonal cocktails don't disappoint. I wouldn't usually trust a gin cocktail to a bar in a hoagie joint, but I was pleasantly surprised to find myself dreaming of English garden parties on a cold first day of winter. My guy ordered a dirty vodka martini on the whim of a craving & it was executed to his taste: not too dirty, not just vodka with some olives. The food really stands out here. The menu is huge (HUGE), & there is something for everyone. I struggle to choose each time I'm in because the chicken cutlet sammies are drool-worthy (my guy literally thinks about them all day), but the hoagies (including the meatless options) are also memorably delightful. Everything is just so fresh, you can tell that this establishment is run by a family that cares about quality & cares about you.

text_raw: On a warm day with a breeze, we found this brewpub in downtown Fishers and were pleased to see it had a huge patio. After parking in their lot on the west side of the brewery, we checked in at the hostess stand and then headed out to a table in the covered area of the patio. This place is clean, spacious, and has a welcoming vibe like being invited into someone's home....a very big home! Since we had lunch before arriving, I decided to order four of their 5 oz brews ($2.25 each) to make a flight. I went with the Coffee Blonde (4.8% 20 IBU), the Blood Orange Blonde "BOB" (4.8% 20 IBU), Brick Arch Porter (6.5% 30 IBU), and Mofo Risin' Stout (4.8% 27 IBU). Of the four, the "BOB" was the most memorable. I really liked how the citrus flavor of the Blood Orange seemed to blend with the blonde flavors of the ale. I would definitely order a pint of this! The others had a lot of coffee and/or chocolate undertones. My wife decided to skip the ales and head straight to the dessert menu. She ordered an ice cream cookie sandwich. This week's combo was a peanut butter cookie filled with chocolate ice cream and drizzled with chocolate syrup. The best part of it was that she shared! It was really delicious, and fortunately, the last two beers on my list had chocolate notes already and paired well with the dessert. There are lots of added touches to the place. A cool mural on the west side of the building has a railroad theme. The chairs and tables on the patio were matched and felt very comfortable. In the center of the patio is an "island" table/bar with the center of the island filled with stone and oil lamps. There was even seating on the east side of the building where the brewery tanks are located for those who want a more industrial vibe. Although we live on the other side of the metro area, my wife has already mentioned taking friends with us on a return visit to try out the dinner menu.Review #326

My hubby got a beer and we got roasted brussel sprouts and mozzarella cheese sticks for an app. Unfortunately it was a good 25 minutes before these came out. Long enough to have a refill on our drinks. The Moz cheese sticks were excellent. The panko crumbs they were rolled in had a phenomenal crispness to them. The flavor was excellent. The cheese was thoroughly melted. It was perfect in every way you wanted your cheese stick to look and taste. The marinara and ranch dipping sauce was also excellent. They make their own house marinara and it is excellent warmed up. Also, the ranch was excellent too. Not just a salad dressing ranch, but a very tasty peppery ranch. Overall, moz sticks a success! Brussel sprouts were ok. The actual sprout was roasted and tasted ok, still slightly bitter though. To counter that it was served in a bowl of yogurt. It wasn't cohesive, it didn't seem like it fit well together, and seemed like an odd dish overall. It was ok if you like your sprouts a little bitter. For pizza, I got the Margarita pizza and my hubby got the White Tiger. It took about an hour to get this after we ordered it. That was the down side. On the plus side, it was delicious!!! I loved the fresh basil and mozzarella on mine. The ratio was a little light for me, but the over taste was excellent. The only thing I'd change is a bit more moz and basil. I felt it was too spread out and not enough cheese to cover the pizza. But taste was exactly what I had wanted. My hubby loved his white tiger. The sausage and caramelized onions were excellent. The one change he suggested was for the garlic to be chopped up instead of whole garlic cloves on the pizza. Overall food was excellent, however wait time for food could really be improved. Overall customer service was excellent too.

text_raw: While a little on the pricey side, Fork: etc. is one part of the coffee shop triumvirate in Old City. There are 3 highlights for coffee in this area: Cafe Ole, Old City Coffee, and Fork: etc. I will say that in recent history, I've been a little disappointed with Old City. Ole still holds my top spot, but after a really nice visit to Fork: etc., I can see why it has a loyal following. First of all, they serve La Colombe, which is the quickest way to my heart. On the side of my coffee, I had a molasses and ginger cookie, which was incredible. Their breakfast and lunch options looked very nice as well, but the only downside would be the cost. Old City is the main tourist drag - the bell-gazing thoroughfare as I like to call it - and as such, places like Fork are going to bump up their prices a bit. For us Philly yokels, it can be hard to justify spending 10-15 bucks on a coffee and a small bite.But I'm here to review the quality. And with the friendliness of its servers and the substance of its dishes - carried 10 feet over from the kitchen naturally shared with Fork, the main restaurant - I'd say this is a worthy stopover. If you're a visitor to Philly and you can't make it to the La Colombe by city hall (15th and Ranstead), definitely grab a coffee at Fork: etc. La Colombe is one of the great exports of Philadelphia, and one of the best cups of coffee I've ever tasted.

text_raw: I just got back my dinner at Gyu-Kaku. They only opened on Friday, so there was already a bit of a line when they opened at 5:00 PM tonight. Thankfully my husband and I only had to wait about fifteen minutes, so that wasn't so bad. I would recommend making a reservation in the future though. I've seen this chain in Japan, but had never gone there since I thought they really only offered grilled gyu niku (beef). However, after hearing they were opening in Philly and seeing their menu with lots of seafood, chicken, and veggies options and the fact that they had chu-hi's (a shochu cocktail), and green tea crepe cake, I figured I had to check it out.The menu is divided into sections. The first part is prepared items from the kitchen such as dumplings, salads, and some fried foods. The next two pages after that are uncooked meat and veggies that you order with a sauce of your choice such as garlic, tare (soy based sauce), basil, miso, or teriyaki sauce and cook at the grill that's built into your table. The last page has a few more ready items from the kitchen, plus a few desserts. Alcohol is on a separate page and include Japanese beers, sake, shochu, and a variety of cocktails. Our server recommended 3-4 items per person in order to get full. Here's the break down of what we had:*Addicting Cucumber - This was the most disappointing dish of the evening. I was hoping for tsukemono (Japanese pickles). However it was just some cubes of cucumber with a little salt and soy sauce on it. Meh.*Fried Shrimp Dumplings - Crispy and full of shrimp. I really liked these. I wasn't a fan of the spicy mayo it was served with though.*Fried Bacon Chips - My husband ordered these. He enjoyed them with the dipping salt and said it surprisingly wasn't too salty.*Chicken - We got the recommended teriyaki sauce. These pieces are small and cut thin, so it takes about one minute per side to grill these. *Salmon- At first they told us they were sold out, but the then waiter checked and they had some. It comes in a foil packet, so it doesn't stick to the grill. This took a while to cook. We had to check it and re-wrap it a few times. It was nice with the ponzu (citrus) sauce that was on the table.*Shrimp with Garlic Sauce - Really good, big meaty shrimp. Can't go wrong here.*Assorted Veggies - You get a little of everything -- corn, peppers, onions, mushrooms, and corn. It's a good value. We really liked the corn. *Mushroom Medley - It comes in foil and is mostly shitake and enoki mushrooms. They were very flavorful. If you like mushrooms, this is a must.*DRINKS* - My calpico (a Japanese soft drink) chu-hi tasted just like Japan. The green tea chu-hi was nice as the tea wasn't sweetened. I was hoping for matcha, but it is just green tea.I really, really wanted the green tea crepe cake. However, the manager informed me that only one place on the east coast makes it, and it's in NYC. They will deliver on Thursdays, so if you want a piece, your best bet is to come in Thursday or Friday. I will be back for this.The service was good, and the manager came to check on us a few times. We got 20% off our entire check for coming during opening week, which I thought was a nice gesture. The food isn't mind-blowing, but it's pretty tasty. I really enjoyed it, and I don't even eat gyu-niku (beef)! The main attraction is the grilling concept that is fun, and reminded me of barbeques I used to attend when I lived in Japan. It's nice to have a selection of sake and shochu as well. I hope Philadelphia starts to get more authentic Japanese restaurants like these in the future. Then I can save a lot of money instead of having to go to NYC every time I'm missing Japan.
